# Accession numbers, decoded {#sec-accessions}

Every record in these databases has an **accession**: a prefix that says
what kind of thing it is, and a number. Once you can read the prefixes, you
can tell from an ID alone whether it's a project, a sample, or the reads.

## The hierarchy

From largest to smallest:

| Level | GEO | SRA (NCBI) | ENA | DDBJ | BioProject / BioSample | Airway example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Project / study** | `GSE` | `SRP` | `ERP` | `DRP` | `PRJNA`, `PRJEB`, `PRJDB` | GSE52778, SRP033351, PRJNA229998 |
| **Biological sample** | `GSM` | `SRS` | `ERS` | `DRS` | `SAMN`, `SAMEA`, `SAMD` | GSM1275862, SAMN02422669 |
| **Experiment** (one library) | | `SRX` | `ERX` | `DRX` | | SRX384345 |
| **Run** (the reads) | | **`SRR`** | **`ERR`** | **`DRR`** | | **SRR1039508** |

**Runs are what you download.** `prefetch` and `fasterq-dump` work on run
accessions (`SRR`/`ERR`/`DRR`). If you give `prefetch` a higher-level ID
(an `SRP` or `SRX`), it will usually work out the runs, but it's clearer to
make the run list yourself.

## Sample, library, run: what's the difference? {#sample-library-run}

Three words that sound alike but mean different things, from the bench to the
sequencer:

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart LR
  S["Sample<br/>the biological material<br/>(a well of cells, a mouse liver)<br/>GSM · SRS · SAMN"] -->|"extract RNA/DNA,<br/>library prep"| L["Library<br/>the tube of adapter-ligated<br/>fragments made from it<br/>SRX (experiment)"]
  L -->|"load on a<br/>flow cell"| R["Run<br/>one batch of reads from<br/>sequencing that library<br/>SRR · ERR · DRR"]
```

| | **Sample** | **Library** | **Run** |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | The biological thing you collected: cells, tissue, a treatment condition, a replicate | The sequencing-ready molecules **made from** a sample's RNA or DNA with one protocol | The reads that came off the sequencer for one library on one lane / flow cell / sequencing batch |
| Made by | Your experiment | Library prep (e.g. TruSeq Stranded mRNA, ATAC, CUT&Tag) | The sequencer |
| Accessions | GEO `GSM`, SRA `SRS`, BioSample `SAMN` | SRA `SRX` ("experiment") | `SRR` / `ERR` / `DRR` |
| Can there be several per parent? | — | Yes: one sample → several libraries (RNA-seq and ATAC from the same cells; or the same prep done twice) | Yes: one library → several runs (several lanes, a re-sequencing to add depth) |
| In a replicate design | **Biological replicates** = different samples | **Technical replicates** = different libraries from one sample | Lanes / top-ups: **not** replicates, just more reads |
| bagPipes samplesheet column | `Bio_Rep` | `Tech_Rep` | `Seq_Rep` |
| What to do before analysis | Keep separate: each is a data point | Usually merge, after checking they look alike | **Always merge** (concatenate FASTQs) |

A quick test: **if it went through a different pipette tip at the bench, it's
a different sample or library; if it only went through a different lane of the
sequencer, it's the same library, just another run.**

## Runs, experiments and samples are not always one-to-one

```
GSM (sample)  ──  SRX (one library from it)  ──┬── SRR  (lane 1)
                                               ├── SRR  (lane 2)
                                               └── SRR  (a re-sequencing)
```

- One **sample** can have several **experiments** (e.g. two libraries
  from the same RNA).
- One **experiment** (library) can have several **runs**: different lanes
  or flow cells, or extra sequencing to add depth.

In the airway data each GSM has exactly one SRR. In many datasets it doesn't,
and then **all the runs of a library need to be joined** before analysis, or
you'll treat lanes as if they were separate replicates. See
[Verify and organise](verify-organise.qmd#one-sample-many-runs).

## Other IDs you'll meet

| ID | What |
|---|---|
| `SUB...` | A submission ID, only meaningful to the submitter |
| `GPL...` | GEO platform (the sequencer type, e.g. GPL11154 = Illumina HiSeq 2000, *Homo sapiens*) |
| `GDS...` | An old curated GEO dataset; ignore for sequencing |
| `phs...` | dbGaP study (controlled access) |
| `EGAD`, `EGAS` | EGA dataset / study (controlled access) |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding

1. A lab grows cells in three separate dishes, makes one RNA-seq library from
   each, and sequences each library on two lanes. How many samples, libraries
   and runs is that, and how many rows go in the samplesheet?
2. Which of these can you pass to `fasterq-dump`: `GSM1275862`, `SRX384345`,
   `SRR1039508`, `PRJNA229998`?
3. A GSM links to one SRX, which has four SRRs. How many samples should be in
   your samplesheet for it?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Answers

1. 3 samples, 3 libraries, 6 runs. Three samplesheet rows: join the two lanes
   of each library first.
2. Only the run accession, `SRR1039508`. (An `ERR` or `DRR` run would work too.)
3. One. The four runs are the same library sequenced four times (lanes or
   top-ups), so join them into one pair of FASTQ files.
:::
:::
